edits.content:
## Mandatory answer line (write this FIRST, before the answer tags)
`Type: <what the clue's 'this X' / quote / title asks for> | Evidence: <quoted passage line or own fact> | Check: <candidate put into the clue's blank reads correctly, is that type, is not a clue word, matches the clue's singular/plural, and fits one distinctive clue detail>`
- A bare 'Title + Name' clue -> Type is what that person leads (country, organization), never a role phrase like 'President of X'. A quote clue -> Type is the speaker; give the famous surname form, never a first name alone.
- If Check fails, change the candidate and rewrite the line. Never output a candidate that fails it.

edits.target: ## Rule 1: Questions are Jeopardy-style clues; always answer with the missing entity
edits.content:
- DEFINITION / ETYMOLOGY CLUES: a clue that merely describes a category ('A house with floors that differ by about half a story', 'An astringent applied under the arms') or glosses a word ('comes from the Latin for "before behind"', 'means "servant of Allah"') asks for the standard NAME or headword the passages pair with that description. Do not answer with (a) a paraphrase of the clue, (b) one example, ingredient or remedy of the category, (c) a prefix or fragment of the word, or (d) an unrelated passage phrase. Choose the term repeated across passages next to the clue's key words, check it fits the whole description, and give only that word with no gloss.
- ACRONYMS: if the clue contains an acronym or abbreviation ('If your TV has PIP, it has this feature'), the answer is usually its spelled-out expansion, which the passages gloss. This is the one case where reusing the clue's own letters is correct.

edits.target: If the list is of real people, answer with the team, state or other entity they share.
edits.content: If the list is of real people or office-holders (kings, presidents, players), answer with the ONE country, dynasty, team, state or institution they share, never one of the listed names or a regnal form of one.

edits.target: and answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content:
Further wordplay and variant clues:
  - SPOONERISM: if the clue says someone 'once talked of / said' a garbled phrase (Dr. Spooner), the answer is the INTENDED phrase obtained by swapping the initial sounds of the clue's words, not a person it was aimed at.
  - SAME ENTITY, DIFFERENT YEARS OR EPITHETS: when the clue gives two roles, epithets or years for one character, the answer is the base name both versions share (usually the first name), without the epithet words the clue already states.
  - DESCRIPTOR ON 'THIS X': a qualifier attached to 'this <noun>' ('found in Florida', 'rare') must fit the answer. If a passage echoes the clue by naming a relative or associate of the anchor that does not satisfy the qualifier, choose the entity that does.

edits.target: ## Rule 3: Look for the clue repeated verbatim in the context
edits.content:
- PARSE ARCHIVE LINES STRICTLY: in 'CLUE | ANSWER. right: Name. wrong: Name.' the answer is ONLY the text immediately after the clue's '|' and before '. right:'. Any name after 'right:' or 'wrong:' is a quiz CONTESTANT and is NEVER the answer (not even a bare first name). If you were about to answer with a name taken from after 'right:' or 'wrong:', stop and take the text before it instead.
- Copy the archive answer character for character, including parenthesised optional parts and surname-only or short forms. Do not strip parentheses or add a first name. Name-normalisation rules apply only when no archive answer exists. If one snippet shows the clue without the answer (a truncated list page), look for the same clue in another passage (flashcards, J! Archive) that includes it.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - No verbatim hit? Look for a passage sentence or dictionary-style definition that PARAPHRASES the clue's distinctive predicate ('a coin... worth one twentieth of a pound'). The headword being defined, or the word filling the slot in that sentence, is the answer. Take it from the paraphrase that matches the most clue details, even when other passages are about a different topic.

edits.target: ## Rule 2: Answer the referent, not a word from the clue
edits.content:
- 'this way', 'in this manner', 'like this', 'how' ('when you play it this way, X happens') ask for the MANNER: an adverb or short phrase. The results listed in the clue are consequences and anchors, never the answer. Find the passage that completes 'play it ___' / 'do it ___' and copy that word.
- RELATIVE CLUES ('his grandfather, the adding machine inventor, would have...', 'her mother, the novelist') and PAIR CLUES ('<Name> & this actor', 'daughter of <Name> & this playwright'): the named relative or partner is only a hint. The answer is the PERSON who owns that relative, or the OTHER member of the pair, whom the passages tie to the anchor and who matches the role noun and the rest of the clue. Passages often name the relative prominently (often sharing a surname); do not copy that name or the anchor. A same-film actress is not 'this actor'.

edits.target: - Example pattern: a clue about a region 'in this country' wants the country, not the region. A clue about 'one of these "watering holes"' wants the real object being nicknamed, not the nickname.
- Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - A topic word that fills the passages (a treaty, a product, a program) or a named item in the clue is an ANCHOR, never the answer: 'this country's <award>' -> the country, not the award or a region; '<character> in this play' -> the play; '<dispute> ... this Texas city' -> the city, not the treaty; 'one of these "watering holes"' -> the real object, not the nickname. Answer with the entity of the stated category that the passages repeatedly pair with the anchor, in its short standard form.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - When a brand, series or topic has many famous members (a snack maker's products, a band's songs), do not default to the most famous one. Choose the member the passages tie to the clue's distinctive detail or caption, and quote that passage detail in your reasoning. Verify one distinctive clue fact (team, size, superlative, year) against your candidate before committing.

edits.target: - When the clue says only 'one of these' / 'this <generic noun>' and the answer is a common noun, give the plain common noun with no added modifiers: 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'). Modifiers copied from passages (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) are usually wrong unless part of the standard proper name.
edits.content: - FINAL ECHO CHECK (substitution test): put your candidate into the clue's blank. If it repeats a noun the clue already states, or is the wrong kind of thing for the clue's 'this <type>' (a conference when the clue asks for a city, a base when it asks for an acid), reject it. When the clue gives a generic noun ('one of these', 'this <noun>') and the leftover is itself a noun that works alone as standard shorthand (bear, bull, pyre), drop the head noun: 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'). Keep the head noun only when the clue's own 'this <type>' IS the head of the standard name and the leftover is an adjective, place, surname or modifier that cannot name the thing alone ('Roman Empire', 'Gadsden Purchase', 'pituitary gland', a quoted head word such as a '...point' whose modifier alone is not a name). This exception never applies when the clue's noun is a different category from the answer (city, acid, person). Modifiers copied from passages (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) are usually wrong unless part of the standard proper name. A verbatim archive answer (Rule 3) still wins.

edits.target: - Use the shortest standard form that names the entity, as a trivia answer key would. If the clue says 'this vitamin', answer with just the letter. If the clue names a group or band, give the group's name only. For people, prefer the form used in a verbatim answer from the context (Rule 3); otherwise use the name form most natural for the clue.
